member.name: F:GrapeCity.Win.Views.DateView.DateDropDownHolder._useDefaultCapturePolicy
member.summary: Indicates whether use default capture policy.
member.remarks:
The default value is "true". This means that the drop-down window will be closed once it losts caputure. If this flag set to "false", it means that the default logical link list will be cut off. The caller of this property should be responsible for reconnecting this default logic link list at some time(Just set this property to "true"), otherwise, the drop-down function will be broken.
Note: Maybe the InputComboContainer.DropDownDialog will maintain this property in the future, however, when I offer this property, there is just GcDateTime needs this function(It will support NavigateTip in drop-down calendar). So, I placed it here. If someone finds that there are more and more drop-down controls need this function, then I suggest that move this property and related logic to the InputComboContainer.DropDownDialog class.
--- Aaron commented on 2007-08-16

When setting the BackColor property of your control, ensure that the color you choose does not cause the text of the control to disappear. member.summary: Gets the selection start position.

The value indicates the selection start position.
The default is 0.
member.remarks: If no text is selected in the control, this property indicates the insertion point for new text. If you set this property to a location beyond the length of the text in the control, the selection start position will be placed after the last character. When text is selected in the control, changing this property might decrease the value of the property. If the remaining text in the control after the position indicated by the property is less than the value of the SelectionLength property, the value of the SelectionLength property is automatically decreased. The value of the property never causes an increase in the SelectionLength property.

member.summary: Gets the length of the selection.
member.value:
The length of the selection.
The default is 0.
member.remarks: You can use this property to determine if any characters are currently selected in the control before performing operations on the selected text. When the value of the SelectionLength property is set to a value that is larger than the number of characters within the text of the control, the value of the SelectionLength property is set to the entire length of text within the control minus the value of the property (if any value is specified for the SelectionStart property).

If IsInputChar returns , the specified character is preprocessed and only sent to the control if it is not consumed by the preprocessing phase. The preprocessing of a character includes checking whether the character is a mnemonic of another control.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Spread.InputMan.CellType.GcCharMask.AutoConvert
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to automatically convert the entered characters according to the input mask.
member.value: if characters are automatically converted according to the input mask; otherwise, . The default is .

remarks.para: If set the AutoConvert property to , all convertible characters will be automatically converted accordingly to the input mask. For example, if set the input mask to "A", by hitting a lower case character the control automatically converts the character into an upper case.

If SBCS is entered in a DBCS mask input, the entered character will be automatically converted to DBCS. Also a DBCS space will be automatically converted to a SBCS space when the control allows only SBCS.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Spread.InputMan.CellType.GcCharMask.AllowSpace
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to allow space input.
member.value:
One of the values.
The default is .

remarks.para: Use the AllowSpace property to specify which kind of space will be allowed in the text.

If the AllowSpace is None mode, this GcCharMask will not accept space. The AllowSpace.Narrow means the SBCS space will be allowed. The AllowSpace.Wide means the DBCS space will be allowed. And the AllowSpace.Both means all kinds of space will be allowed.
remarks.note: If the propety is and the AllowSpace is AllowSpace.Wide, the control will auto convert the SBCS space to DBCS space when user input a SBCS space char. It's the same to other settings. And the property always be used with this AllowSpace property.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Spread.InputMan.CellType.GcCharMask.BackColor
member.summary: Gets or sets the background color for the control.
member.value: A that represents the background color of the control.
member.remarks:
You can use the BackColor property to change the background color of the text control to blend into the color scheme of your forms.
To change the color of the text within the control, use the property. member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Spread.InputMan.CellType.GcDateTime.ValidateMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the validation mode during input for the control.
member.value: One of the enumeration values. The default is .
member.exception: A value that is not within the range of valid values for the enumeration was assigned to the property.

remarks.para: If setting the ValidateMode property to , the control will perform strict validation such as checking for leap-years and non-existing date values. Also, automatic character filtering and field adjustments will be made as the user enters data. For example, in the case of leap years, when the input mask is set to 'yyyy.MM.dd', the user will not be able to enter February 29th, 2003. If the input mask is set to 'dd.MM.yyyy', entering February 29th, 2003 will automatically adjust the 29th to the 28th as soon as the last 3 is entered for the year.

If setting this property to ValidateModeEx.Validate, the control will perform loose validation causing all fields to behave independently and not rely on each other. For example, if the input mask is set to 'yyyy.MM.dd', the control allows you to enter a date such as February 31st, 2003 which normally cannot exist as a date-time value. The following table shows the valid range for the fields when the mode is ValidateModeEx.Validate.

If setting this property to , the control does not perform validation. The fields behave independently just as when set to . For example, if the input mask is set to 'yyyy.MM.dd', the control allows you to enter '0000.00.00' which is not a date-time value. The following table shows the valid range for the fields when using :
This property takes effect only when entering data in the control. The date-time value is validated as soon as focus moves away from the control.
During input, if the entered data is incomplete, such as '2003.__.01', or a non date-time value such as '2002.02.31' is entered, the property returns null.
remarks.note: Performing spin actions causes date-time values to change in any mode of the ValidateMode property. The valid range for the spin actions is equivalent to entering data as shown in the tables above.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Win.Spread.InputMan.CellType.GcListBox.BeginUpdate
member.summary: Maintains performance when items are added to the control more than one at a time.
member.remarks: This method prevents the control from layouting and painting until the method is called. The preferred way to add items to the is to use the method of the class (through the Items property of the GcListBox This enables you to add an array of items to the list at one time. However, if you want to add items one at a time using the method of the ListItemCollection class, you can use the BeginUpdate method to prevent the control from repainting the GcListBox each time an item is added to the list. Once you have completed the task of adding items to the list, call the method to enable the GcListBox to repaint. This way of adding items can prevent flicker during the drawing of the GcListBox when a large number of items are being added to the list.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Win.Spread.InputMan.CellType.GcListBox.EndUpdate

member.name: T:GrapeCity.Win.Spread.InputMan.CellType.GcNumber
member.summary: Represents a GcNumber control
member.remarks: The GcNumber control provides number input for positive and negative values and allows you to design a functional numeric input interface quickly and efficiently. During data entry, the user can press the minus sign ("-") at any time to toggle the value between positive and negative. Also, the plus sign ("+") will change a negative value to positive.

This version of the Find method searches for the first instance of a character from a list of characters specified in the characterSet parameter and returns the location of the character. For example, you pass an array of characters containing the character 'Q'. If the control contained the text "The Quick Brown Fox", the Find method would return the value of four. An upper case character and a lower case character are considered different values in the search.
If the property returns a negative value, the characters being searched for were not found within the contents of the control. You can use this method to search for a group of characters within the control. This version of the Find method requires that the entire document contained in the control is searched for the characters. If a character from the character list provided in the method's characterSet parameter is found, the value returned by this method is a zero-based index of the character's position in the control. A space is considered a character by the method when determining the location of a character.

if show selection margin; otherwise, .

member.remarks:
You can use this property to enable the user to easily select lines of text in the . The selection margin is added to the left side of the . This margin makes it easier for the user to select text starting on the left side of the control. The user can click in the selection margin to select a single line of text or double-click to select the entire paragraph that the line double-clicked is contained within.
If the ShowSelectionMargin property is set to true, setting the property to RichTextBoxScrollBars.Horizontal, RichTextBoxScrollBars.Vertical, or RichTextBoxScrollBars.Both will not cause scroll bars to be displayed. In order to display scroll bars while the property is set to true, set the property to RichTextBoxScrollBars.ForcedHorizontal, RichTextBoxScrollBars.ForcedVertical, or RichTextBoxScrollBars.ForcedBoth.

Any text that is entered that extends beyond this margin is placed on the next line of text in the control. This property affects all text currently entered into the control as well as any additional text entered into the control after the property is set. member.name: M:GrapeCity.Win.Views.FieldsEditor.InternalSetKeyDownCache(System.Windows.Forms.KeyEventArgs)
member.summary: Sets the last key down data internally.
member.param: The instance containing the event data.
member.remarks: For internally use only. (Bug ID#431 in IM6). I have to cache the data before fire event to user. Otherwise when KeyPress/KeyUp event received, the caches are invalid. And I have discussed these two flags with Kevin. We used to set these two flag to prevent Ctrl+H take effect. But at last, the policy changed, we don't have to distingush the Backspace key and Ctrl+H keys. So the best choice is to refactor the key process logic the same as it in the GcTextBox. But in current stage, I add this method as a walk-around. ----- Leo commented at 2009.07.28 -----

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Win.Views.BindingData._itemHeightCollection
member.summary: Indicates a collction used to store the height of all the ListItem when data binding.
member.remarks: Used by HandleAutoHeightAndAutoWidthForDataBinding method. The reason why BindingData need this cache is following: The mechanism of data-binding is to use an item template to instead all the ListItems, so, when data-bindign is completed, all the ListItems are referenceed to the item temmplate(Only one instance in the memory). In order to layout all the items rightly, the heights of all the ListItems should be known.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Views.BindingData.RowTemplateForDataBinding
member.summary: Gets a template of ListItem for data binding.
member.value: A value.
member.remarks:
This is a very important data for data-binding. Its content only related with the schema of the data source. So, if the following cases happen, then its content should be recreated or updated at once.
1. The DataSource changed 2. The DataMember changed 3. The ListBindingManager changed 4 Add or remove the Column of data source (NOT DataSource)
In order to get the actual template for ListItem when the GcListbox is data-binding, BindingData will update or create the template once the getter of this property is called.
--- Aaron commented on 2007-08-28

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Bevel.Lightness
member.summary: Gets or sets the percentage used for calculating the color used for the light area of the bevel.
member.value: An integer value (between -100 through 100) that indicates the lighting percentage. (25 as default)

remarks.para: This property bases the color ( property) of the object to calculate the light color for the bevel in percentages.
If set to 0, the same color as the color is used. When a positive value is set, a color brighter, and when a negative value is set, a color darker than the background color will take effect.
This property can be used with the property to make detail adjustments of the brightness of the bevel color.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Bevel.Darkness
member.summary: Gets or sets the percentage used for calculating the color used for the shade area of the bevel.
member.value: An integer value (between -100 through 100) that indicates the shading percentage. (-25 as default)

remarks.para: This property bases the color ( property) of the object to calculate the shade color for the bevel in percentages.
If set to 0, the same color as the color is used. When a positive value is set, a color brighter, and when a negative value is set, a color darker than the color will take effect.
This property can be used with the property to make detail adjustments of the brightness of the bevel color.

member.value: An integer value indicating the width of the bevel. (0 as default)
member.remarks: When a negative value is set to the Width property, the bevel effect will look Inset, and when a positive value is set, the effect will look Raised. A 2D effect can be achieved by setting the Width property to 0 (zero).

member.name: T:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.ColorHLS
member.summary: HLS color space. A mapping of color components onto a Cartesian coordinate system in three or more dimensions.

remarks.newpara: Its color components are hue, lightness, and saturation.
Hue has the same meaning as the HSV model, except that a hue angle of 0?corresponds to blue in this model. Magenta is at 60? red is at 120? As with the HSV model, complementary colors are 180?apart.
Lightness is the amount of black or white in a color. Increasing lightness adds white to the hue. Decreasing lightness adds black to the hue.
Saturation in the HLS model is a measure of the "purity" of a hue. As saturation is decreased, the hue becomes more gray. A saturation value of zero results in a gray-scale value.

member.summary: Logical units are mapped to arbitrary units with arbitrarily scaled axes. Use the WindowExtent and ViewportExtent properties to specify the units, orientation, and scaling.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.DeviceContexts.MappingMode.Isotropic
member.summary: Logical units are mapped to arbitrary units with equally scaled axes; that is, one unit along the x-axis is equal to one unit along the y-axis. Use the WindowExtent and ViewportExtent properties to specify the units and the orientation of the axes. Graphics device interface (GDI) makes adjustments as necessary to ensure the x and y units remain the same size (When the window extent is set, the viewport will be adjusted to keep the units isotropic).

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.DeviceContexts.MappingMode.LoEnglish

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.DeviceContexts.MappingMode.LoMetric

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.DeviceContexts.MappingMode.Text

member.summary: retrieves the foreground mix mode of the specified device context. The mix mode specifies how the pen or interior color and the color already on the screen are combined to yield a new color.

member.summary: Sets the current foreground mix mode. GDI uses the foreground mix mode to combine pens and interiors of filled objects with the colors already on the screen. The foreground mix mode defines how colors from the brush or pen and the colors in the existing image are to be combined.
member.param: Specifies the mix mode. This parameter can be one of the following values.
member.returns: If the function succeeds, the return value specifies the previous mix mode. otherwise, zero indicates failed
member.remarks: Mix modes define how GDI combines source and destination colors when drawing with the current pen. The mix modes are binary raster operation codes, representing all possible Boolean functions of two variables, using the binary operations AND, OR, and XOR (exclusive OR), and the unary operation NOT. The mix mode is for raster devices only; it is not available for vector devices.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.DeviceContexts.DeviceContext.DrawArc(System.Drawing.Point,System.UInt32,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Draws a line segment and an arc. The line segment is drawn from the position which is defined by radius and startAngle. The arc is drawn along the perimeter of a circle with the given radius and center. The length of the arc is defined by the given start and sweep angles.
member.param: A specifies the center of the circle.
A uint specifies the radius of the circle. This value must be positive.
A float specifies the start angle, in degrees.
A float specifies the sweep angle, in degrees, relative to the starting angle.
member.remarks: The arc is drawn by constructing an imaginary circle around the specified center point with the specified radius. The starting point of the arc is determined by measuring counterclockwise from the x-axis of the circle by the number of degrees in the start angle. The ending point is similarly located by measuring counterclockwise from the starting point by the number of degrees in the sweep angle. If the sweep angle is greater than 360 degrees,the arc is swept multiple times.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.DeviceContexts.DeviceContext.DrawArc(System.Drawing.Rectangle,System.Drawing.Point,System.Drawing.Point)
member.summary: Draws an elliptical arc.
member.param: A specifies the bounding rectangle.
A specifies the ending point of the radial line defining the starting point of the arc.
A specifies the ending point of the radial line defining the ending point of the arc.
member.remarks: The rectangle specify the bounding rectangle. An ellipse formed by the specified bounding rectangle defines the curve of the arc. The arc extends in the current drawing direction from the point where it intersects the radial from the center of the bounding rectangle to the firstRadial point. The arc ends where it intersects the radial from the center of the bounding rectangle to the secondRadial point. If the starting point and ending point are the same, a complete ellipse is drawn.

member.summary: Draws a series of line segments by connecting the points in the specified array.
member.param: A array indicates the line segments.

remarks.para:
The lines are drawn from the first point through subsequent points by using the current pen. Windows 95/98/Me: DrawPolyLine cannot draw more than a certain number of points. The limit depends on the line width (that is, the width of the pen selected into the DC)
Line width Maximum points allowed line width is 1 16K line width > 1 (that is, wideline) and device supports wideline 16K line width > 1 but device does not support wideline approximately 1360 (that is, approximately 16K/12)

Any extra points are ignored. To draw a line with more points, divide the data into groups that have less than the maximum number of points and call the function for each group of points. Remember to connect the line segments.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.DeviceContexts.DeviceContext.DrawPolyBezier(System.Drawing.Point[])
member.summary: Draws one or more Bezier curves.
member.param: An array of structures that contain the endpoints and control points of the curve(s). This value must be one more than three times the number of curves to be drawn, because each Bzier curve requires two control points and an endpoint, and the initial curve requires an additional starting point.

remarks.para: DrawPolyBezier draws cubic Bzier curves by using the endpoints and control points specified by the points parameter. The first curve is drawn from the first point to the fourth point by using the second and third points as control points. Each subsequent curve in the sequence needs exactly three more points: the ending point of the previous curve is used as the starting point, the next two points in the sequence are control points, and the third is the ending point.

The lines are drawn from the first point through subsequent points by using the current pen. Windows 95/98/Me: DrawPolyBezier cannot draw more than a certain number of points. The limit depends on the line width (that is, the width of the pen selected into the DC)
Line width Maximum points allowed line width is 1 16K line width > 1 (that is, wideline) and device supports wideline 16K line width > 1 but device does not support wideline approximately 1360 (that is, approximately 16K/12)

Any extra points are ignored. To draw a line with more points, divide the data into groups that have less than the maximum number of points and call the function for each group of points. Remember to connect the line segments.

member.summary: Performs a bit-block transfer of the color data corresponding to a rectangle of pixels from the specified source object into a destination DeviceContext object.
member.param: The source object.
A indicates the destination rectangle.
A indicates the upper-left corner of source rectangle. The width and height of source rectangle are same as the destination rectangle.
A indicates the raster operation code.

remarks.para: Copy only does clipping on the destination DC.

If a rotation or shear transformation is in effect in the source device context, Copy will throw a . If other transformations exist in the source device context (and a matching transformation is not in effect in the destination device context), the rectangle in the destination device context is stretched, compressed, or rotated, as necessary.
If the color formats of the source and destination device contexts do not match, the Copy function converts the source color format to match the destination format.
When an enhanced metafile is being recorded, an error occurs if the source device context identifies an enhanced-metafile device context. it means a would be throw out.
Not all devices support the Copy function. For more information, see the RC_BITBLT raster capability entry in the GetDeviceCaps function as well as the following: MaskBlt, PlgBlt, and StretchBlt.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.DeviceContexts.DeviceContext.RasterOperationCode
member.summary: Get or set the current foreground mix mode.GDI uses the foreground mix mode to combine pens and interiors of filled objects with the colors already on the screen. The foreground mix mode defines how colors from the brush or pen and the colors in the existing image are to be combined.
member.value: Specifies the mix mode. This parameter can be one of the following values.
member.remarks: Mix modes define how GDI combines source and destination colors when drawing with the current pen. The mix modes are binary raster operation codes, representing all possible Boolean functions of two variables, using the binary operations AND, OR, and XOR (exclusive OR), and the unary operation NOT. The mix mode is for raster devices only; it is not available for vector devices.

member.summary: Gets or sets the handle of the current clipping region of the device context.
member.value: A that indicates the handle of the clipping region.

remarks.para: Note: [Get] The getting region is a copy of the current region. [Set] Only a copy of the setting region is used. The region itself can be seted for any number of other device contexts or it can be deleted.
To remove a device-context's clipping region, specify a IntPtr.Zero region handle.
The coordinate of region will not be effected by current origin of page space.

member.summary: Initialize a new
member.param: A null-terminated string that specifies the typeface name of the font. The length of this string must not exceed 32 characters, including the terminating null character. The EnumFontFamiliesEx function can be used to enumerate the typeface names of all currently available fonts. If faceName is an empty string, GDI uses the first font that matches the other specified attributes.
Specifies the family of the font

Specifies the height, in logical units, of the font's character cell or character. The character height value (also known as the em height) is the character cell height value minus the internal-leading value.
Specifies the angle, in tenths of degrees, between the escapement vector and the x-axis of the device. The escapement vector is parallel to the base line of a row of text.

Specifies the average width, in logical units, of characters in the font. If width is zero, the aspect ratio of the device is matched against the digitization aspect ratio of the available fonts to find the closest match, determined by the absolute value of the difference.

Specifies the weight of the font in the range 0 through 1000. For example, 400 is normal and 700 is bold. If this value is zero, a default weight is used. The following values are defined for convenience.
Specifies an italic font if set to true.
Specifies an underlined font if set to true.
Specifies a strikeout font if set to true.
Specifies the angle, in tenths of degrees, between each character's base line and the x-axis of the device.
Specifies the character set.
Specifies the output precision. The output precision defines how closely the output must match the requested font's height, width, character orientation, escapement, pitch, and font type.
Specifies the clipping precision. The clipping precision defines how to clip characters that are partially outside the clipping region. It can be one or more of the following values.
Specifies the output quality. The output quality defines how carefully the graphics device interface (GDI) must attempt to match the logical-font attributes to those of an actual physical font.
Specifies the pitch of the font

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.FontBuilder.Height
member.summary: Get or set the height, in logical units, of the font's character cell or character. The character height value (also known as the em height) is the character cell height value minus the internal-leading value.
member.value:
An int indicate the height
if value larger than zero, the font mapper transforms this value into device units and matches it against the cell height of the available fonts.
if value equal zero, the font mapper uses a default height value when it searches for a match.
if value less than zero, the font mapper transforms this value into device units and matches its absolute value against the character height of the available fonts.

member.value: An int indicate the average width

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.FontBuilder.Escapement
member.summary: Get or set the angle, in tenths of degrees, between the escapement vector and the x-axis of the device. The escapement vector is parallel to the base line of a row of text.
member.value: An int indicate the escapement vector

remarks.para: Windows NT/2000/XP: When the graphics mode is set to GM_ADVANCED, you can specify the escapement angle of the string independently of the orientation angle of the string's characters.
When the graphics mode is set to GM_COMPATIBLE, Escapement specifies both the escapement and orientation. You should set Escapement and Orientation to the same value.
Windows 95/98/Me: The Escapement member specifies both the escapement and orientation. You should set Escapement and Orientation to the same value.

summary.p: When this value is used, the rotation for all fonts depends on whether the orientation of the coordinate system is left-handed or right-handed.

member.name: T:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.FontQuality
member.summary: Represents the quality of font.
member.remarks: The output quality defines how carefully the graphics device interface (GDI) must attempt to match the logical-font attributes to those of an actual physical font. It can be one of the following values.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.FontQuality.Default
member.summary: Appearance of the font does not matter.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.FontQuality.Draft
member.summary: Appearance of the font is less important than when Draft is used. For GDI raster fonts, scaling is enabled, which means that more font sizes are available, but the quality may be lower. Bold, italic, underline, and strikeout fonts are synthesized if necessary.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.FontQuality.Proof
member.summary: Character quality of the font is more important than exact matching of the logical-font attributes. For GDI raster fonts, scaling is disabled and the font closest in size is chosen. Although the chosen font size may not be mapped exactly when Proof is used, the quality of the font is high and there is no distortion of appearance. Bold, italic, underline, and strikeout fonts are synthesized if necessary.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.FontQuality.Nonantialiased
member.summary: Font is never antialiased.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.FontQuality.Antialiased
member.summary: Font is always antialiased if the font supports it and the size of the font is not too small or too large.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.FontQuality.ClearType

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.Graphics.DrawArc(GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.Pen,System.Drawing.Rectangle,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Draw the special arc by using the given pen
member.param: A indicate the draw-style of arc
A indicates the bounding rectangle which center is the center of ellipse
A float specifies the start angle, in degrees.
A float specifies the sweep angle, in degrees, relative to the starting angle.
member.remarks: The arc is drawn by constructing an imaginary circle around the specified center point with the specified radius. The starting point of the arc is determined by measuring counterclockwise from the x-axis of the circle by the number of degrees in the start angle. The ending point is similarly located by measuring counterclockwise from the starting point by the number of degrees in the sweep angle. If the sweep angle is greater than 360 degrees,the arc is swept multiple times.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.Graphics.DrawBeziers(GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.Pen,System.Drawing.Point[])
member.summary: Draw the special Bezier curve on current Graphics by using the special pen.
member.param: A indicate the draw-style of Bezier curve

An array of structures that contain the endpoints and control points of the curve(s). This value must be one more than three times the number of curves to be drawn, because each Bzier curve requires two control points and an endpoint, and the initial curve requires an additional starting point.

remarks.para: DrawBeziers draws cubic Bzier curves by using the endpoints and control points specified by the points parameter. The first curve is drawn from the first point to the fourth point by using the second and third points as control points. Each subsequent curve in the sequence needs exactly three more points: the ending point of the previous curve is used as the starting point, the next two points in the sequence are control points, and the third is the ending point.

Any extra points are ignored. To draw a line with more points, divide the data into groups that have less than the maximum number of points and call the function for each group of points. Remember to connect the line segments.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.Graphics.Copy(GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.Graphics,System.Drawing.Rectangle,System.Drawing.Point)
member.summary: Performs a bit-block transfer of the color data corresponding to a rectangle of pixels from the specified source object into a destination Graphics object.
member.param: A indicate the source Graphics object
A indicates the destination rectangle.
A indicates the upper-left corner of source rectangle. The width and height of source rectangle are same as the destination rectangle.

remarks.para: Copy only does clipping on the destination DC.

If a rotation or shear transformation is in effect in the source device context, Copy will throw a . If other transformations exist in the source device context (and a matching transformation is not in effect in the destination device context), the rectangle in the destination device context is stretched, compressed, or rotated, as necessary.
If the color formats of the source and destination device contexts do not match, the Copy function converts the source color format to match the destination format.
When an enhanced metafile is being recorded, an error occurs if the source device context identifies an enhanced-metafile device context. it means a would be throw out.
Not all devices support the Copy function. For more information, see the RC_BITBLT raster capability entry in the GetDeviceCaps function as well as the following: MaskBlt, PlgBlt, and StretchBlt.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.Pen.DrawBeziers(GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.DeviceContexts.DeviceContext,System.Drawing.Point[])
member.summary: Draws one or more Bezier curves.
member.param: A indicate the drawing target

An array of structures that contain the endpoints and control points of the curve(s). This value must be one more than three times the number of curves to be drawn, because each Bzier curve requires two control points and an endpoint, and the initial curve requires an additional starting point.

remarks.para: DrawBeziers draws cubic Bzier curves by using the endpoints and control points specified by the points parameter. The first curve is drawn from the first point to the fourth point by using the second and third points as control points. Each subsequent curve in the sequence needs exactly three more points: the ending point of the previous curve is used as the starting point, the next two points in the sequence are control points, and the third is the ending point.

Any extra points are ignored. To draw a line with more points, divide the data into groups that have less than the maximum number of points and call the function for each group of points. Remember to connect the line segments.

member.name: T:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.Region
member.summary: Represent the interior of a graphics shape composed of rectangles.

remarks.newpara: A region is scalable because its coordinates are specified in world coordinates. On a drawing surface, however, its interior is dependent on the size and shape of the pixels representing it. An application can use regions to clamp the output of drawing operations. The window manager uses regions to define the drawing area of these regions are called clipping regions. An application can also use regions in hit-testing operations, such as checking whether a point or a rectangle intersects a region. An application can fill a region by using a object.

newpara.note: This class uses the Win32 GDI API's for handling regions. The GDI+ version class just seems to be buggy and too slow.

member.summary: Specifies the display and layout information for text strings.

member.summary: No any flags.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.StringFormatFlags.LineLimit
member.summary: Only entire lines are laid out in the formatting rectangle. By default layout continues until the end of the text, or until no more lines are visible as a result of clipping, whichever comes first. Note that the default settings allow the last line to be partially obscured by a formatting rectangle that is not a whole multiple of the line height. To ensure that only whole lines are seen, specify this value and be careful to provide a formatting rectangle at least as tall as the height of one line.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.StringFormatFlags.MultiLine
member.summary: Shows string on one or more lines.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.StringFormatFlags.NoWrap
member.summary: Disables wrapping of text between lines when formatting within a rectangle. This flag is implied when a point is passed instead of a rectangle, or when the specified rectangle has a zero line length.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.StringFormatFlags.WordWrap
member.summary: Breaks words. Lines are automatically broken between words if a word would extend past the edge of the pecified rectangle. A carriage return-line feed sequence also breaks the line.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.StringFormatFlags.RightToLeft
member.summary: Specifies that text is right to left.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.StringFormatFlags.Vertical
member.summary: Specifies that text is vertical.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.StringFormatFlags.NoClip
member.summary: Overhanging parts of glyphs, and unwrapped text reaching outside the formatting rectangle are allowed to show. By default all text and glyph parts reaching outside the formatting rectangle are clipped.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.StringFormatFlags.ExpandTabs
member.summary: Expands tab characters. The default number of characters per tab is eight.

member.name: T:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.StringAlignment
member.summary: Specifies the alignment of a text string relative to its layout rectangle.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.StringAlignment.Center
member.summary: Specifies that text is aligned in the center of the layout rectangle.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.StringAlignment.Far
member.summary: Specifies that text is aligned far from the origin position of the layout rectangle. In a left-to-right layout, the far position is right. In a right-to-left layout, the far position is left.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Gdi.StringAlignment.Near
member.summary: Specifies the text be aligned near the layout. In a left-to-right layout, the near position is left. In a right-to-left layout, the near position is right.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Renders.TextFormat.LineLimit
member.summary:
Gets and sets a value only entire lines are laid out in the formatting rectangle.
By default layout continues until the end of the text, or until no more lines are visible as a result of clipping, whichever comes first.
Note that the default settings allow the last line to be partially obscured by a formatting rectangle that is not a whole multiple of the line height.
To ensure that only whole lines are seen, specify this value and be careful to provide a formatting rectangle at least as tall as the height of one line.
member.remarks: Only when CompatibleRendering is true, this property will take effect.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Renders.TextFormat.MeasureTrailingSpace
member.summary:
Gets and sets a value A value indicates includes the trailing space at the end of each line.
By default the boundary rectangle returned by the MeasureString method excludes the space at the end of each line. Set this flag to include that space in measurement.
member.remarks: Only when CompatibleRendering is true, this property will take effect.

member.remarks:
A image will be measure off nine part, and only some specifies parts can stretch out and draw back.
0| 1| 2 --|--|-- 3| 4| 5 --|--|-- 6| 7| 8
The 0, 2, 6, 8 parts will fixed size. The 1, 7 parts will stretch out and draw back at horizontal direction. The 3, 5 parts will stretch out and draw back at vertical direction. The 4 part will stretch out and draw back at horizontal and vertical direction.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Control.DefualtLanguage
member.summary: Specifies the language to use when Unicode values are ambiguous. This is a LANGID, including both a primary language and a sublanguage. Used by numeric processing to select digit shape when DigitSubstitute of is set.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Control.ContextDigits
member.summary: Specifies that national digits are chosen according to the nearest previous strong text, rather than using DefaultLanguage.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Control.InvertPreBoundDir
member.summary: By default, text at the start of the string is laid out as if it follows a strong LTR character if the base embedding level is 0, and as if it follows a strong RTL character if the base embedding level is 1.Set InvertPreBoundDir to change the initial context to the opposite of the base embedding level. This member is for GetCharacterPlacement legacy support.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Control.InvertPostBoundDir
member.summary: By default, text at the end of the string is laid out as if it precedes strong text of the same direction as the base embedding level. Set InvertPreBoundDir to change the final context to the opposite of the base embedding level. This flag is for GetCharacterPlacement legacy support.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Control.LinkStringBefore
member.summary: Causes the first character of the string to be shaped as if it were joined to a previous character.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Control.LinkStringAfter
member.summary: Causes the last character of the string to be shaped as if it were joined to a following character.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Control.NeutralOverride
member.summary: Causes all neutral characters in the string to be treated as if they were strong characters of their enclosing embedding level. This effectively locks them in place, and reordering occurs only between neutrals.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Control.NumericOverride
member.summary: Causes all numeric characters in the string to be treated as if they were strong characters of their enclosing embedding level. This effectively locks them in place, and reordering occurs only between numeric characters.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Control.LegacyBidiClass
member.summary:
Causes the plus and minus characters to be treated as neutral characters, that is, with no implied direction, and the slash character to be treated as a common separator.
Windows XP: The plus and minus characters are treated as European separators.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.State.BidiLevel
member.summary: The embedding level associated with all characters in this run according to the Unicode bidirectional algorithm. When passed to ScriptItemize, should be initialized to zero for an LTR base embedding level, or 1 for RTL.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.State.OverrideDirection
member.summary: true if this level is an override level (LRO/RLO). In an override level, characters are laid out in one direction only, either left-to-right or right-to-left. No reordering of digits or strong characters of opposing direction takes place. Note that this initial value is reset by LRE, RLE, LRO or RLO codes in the string.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.State.InhibitSymSwap
member.summary: True if the shaping engine is to bypass mirroring of Unicode mirrored glyphs such as brackets. Set by Unicode character ISS, cleared by ASS.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.State.CharShape
member.summary: true if character codes in the Arabic Presentation Forms areas of Unicode should be shaped. (Not implemented).

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.State.DigitSubstitute
member.summary: true if character codes U+0030 through U+0039 (European digits) are to be substituted by national digits. Set by Unicode NADS, cleared by NODS.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.State.InhibitLigate
member.summary: true if ligatures are not to be used in the shaping of Arabic or Hebrew characters.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.State.DisplayZWG
member.summary: true if control characters are to be shaped as representational glyphs. (Typically, control characters are shaped to the blank glyph and given a width of zero).

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Analysis.Script
member.summary:
Opaque value identifying which engine Uniscribe will use when calling the ScriptShape, ScriptPlace, and ScriptTextOut functions for this item. The value of eScript is undefined and will change in future releases, but attributes of eScript may be obtained by calling ScriptGetProperties.
To disable shaping, set this parameter to Analysis.UndefinedScript.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Analysis.RTL
member.summary: Rendering direction. Normally identical to the parity of the Unicode embedding level, but it may differ if overridden by GetCharacterPlacement legacy support.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Analysis.LayoutRTL
member.summary: Logical direction, whether left-to-right or right-to-left. Although this is usually the same as fRTL, for a number in a RTL run, fRTL is False (because digits are always displayed LTR), but fLayoutRTL is True (because the number is read as part of the RTL sequence).

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Analysis.LinkBefore
member.summary: If set, the shaping engine will shape the first character of this item as if it were joining with a previous character. Set by ScriptItemize, it may be overridden before calling ScriptShape.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Analysis.LinkAfter
member.summary: If set, the shaping engine will shape the last character of this item as if it were joining with a subsequent character. Set by ScriptItemize, it may be overridden before calling ScriptShape.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Analysis.LogicalOrder
member.summary: If set, the shaping engine will generate all glyph-related arrays in logical order. By default, glyph-related arrays are in visual order, the first array entry corresponding to the leftmost glyph. Set to false by ScriptItemize, it may be overridden before calling ScriptShape.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Analysis.NoGlyphIndex
member.summary:
Typically false. Set to true for bitmap, vector, and device fonts; and for Asian scripts. It may be set to true on input to ScriptShape to disable use of glyphs for this item. Additionally, ScriptShape will set it to true for an hdc containing symbolic, unrecognized, and device fonts.
Disabling glyphing disables complex script shaping. When set, shaping and placing for this item is implemented directly by calls to GetTextExtentExPoint and ExtTextOut.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.LanguageId
member.summary: Primary language and sublanguage associated with the script. When a script is used for many languages, langid represents a default language. For example, Western script is represented by LANG_ENGLISH although it is also used for French, German, and other European languages.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.CharSet
member.summary: The nominal charset associated with the script. This charset may be used in a log font when creating a font suitable for displaying this script. Note that for a new script where no charset is defined, bCharSet may be inappropriate. In this case, DEFAULT_CHARSET should be used instead. See the description of fAmbiguousCharSet.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.Numeric
member.summary: If set, the script contains only digits and the other characters used in writing numbers by the rules of the Unicode bidirectional algorithm. For example, currency symbols, the thousands separator, and the decimal point are classified as numeric when adjacent to or between digits.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.Complex
member.summary: If set, this is a language whose script requires special shaping or layout. If fComplex is false, the script contains no combining characters and requires no contextual shaping or reordering.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.NeedsWordBreaking
member.summary: If set, this is a language whose word break placement requires that the application call ScriptBreak and that word break placement include character positions marked as WordStop in LogicalAttribute. If not set, word break placement is identified by scanning for characters marked as WhiteSpace in LogicalAttribute, or for glyphs marked as Justify == Justification.Blank or Justification.ArabicBlank in VisualAttribute.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.NeedsCaretInfo
member.summary: If set, this is a language that restricts caret placement to cluster boundaries, for example, Thai and Indian. To determine valid caret positions, inspect the CharStop flag in the logical attributes returned by ScriptBreak, or compare adjacent values in the logicClusters array returned by Script.Shape method.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.Control
member.summary: If set, the script contains only control characters. Note, the converse is not necessarily true��not every control character ends up in a Control structure.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.PrivateUseArea
member.summary: If set, the script uses a special set of characters that is privately defined for the Unicode range U+E000 through U+F8FF.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.NeedsCharacterJustify
member.summary: If set, justification for the script is achieved by increasing the space between all letters, not just between words. When performing inter-character justification, insert extra space only after glyphs marked with VisualAttribute. Justify == Justification.Character.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.InvalidGlyph
member.summary: If set, this is a script for which ScriptShape generates an invalid glyph to represent invalid sequences. That is, it generates wgInvalid in the glyph buffer. The glyph index of the invalid glyph for a particular font may be obtained by calling Script.GetFontProperties method.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.InvalidLogicalAttribute
member.summary: If set, this is a script for which Script.Break marks invalid combinations by setting fInvalid in the logical attributes buffer.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.CDM
member.summary: If set, the script contains an item that was analyzed by Script.Itemize as including Combining Diacritical Marks (U+0300 through U+36F).

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.AmbiguousCharSet
member.summary: If set, the script contains characters that are supported by more than one charset. See the Remarks section for more information. The bCharSet member should be set to DEFAULT_CHARSET.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.ClusterSizeVaries
member.summary: If set, this is a script, such as Arabic, in which contextual shaping may cause a string to increase in size when removing characters. An example of this is Arabic.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Drawing.Uniscribe.Properties.RejectInvalid
member.summary: If set, this is a script, such as Thai, where invalid sequences conventionally cause an editor program��such as Notepad��to beep and ignore keystrokes.

Pointer to an array that receives the logical cluster information. Each element in logicClusters corresponds to a character in run. member.summary: Monitors keystroke messages and triggers key related events.
member.param: Specifies a code the hook procedure uses to determine how to process the message.
Specifies the virtual-key code of the key that generated the keystroke message.
Specifies the repeat count, scan code, extended-key flag, context code, previous key-state flag, and transition-state flag.
member.returns: If code is less than zero, the hook procedure must return the value returned by CallNextHookEx. If code is greater than or equal to zero, and the hook procedure did not process the message, it is highly recommended that you call CallNextHookEx and return the value it returns; otherwise, other applications that have installed WH_KEYBOARD hooks will not receive hook notifications and may behave incorrectly as a result. If the hook procedure processed the message, it may return a nonzero value to prevent the system from passing the message to the rest of the hook chain or the target window procedure.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Platform.UnsafeNativeMethods.EmptyClipboard
member.summary: The EmptyClipboard function empties the clipboard and frees handles to data in the clipboard. The function then assigns ownership of the clipboard to the window that currently has the clipboard open.
member.returns: If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Platform.UnsafeNativeMethods.SetClipboardData(System.UInt32,System.IntPtr)
member.summary: The SetClipboardData function places data on the clipboard in a specified clipboard format.
member.param: Specifies a clipboard format. This parameter can be a registered format or any of the standard clipboard formats.

Handle to the data in the specified format. This parameter can be NULL, indicating that the window provides data in the specified clipboard format (renders the format) upon request. If a window delays rendering, it must process the WM_RENDERFORMAT and WM_RENDERALLFORMATS messages.
member.returns: If the function succeeds, the return value is the handle to the data. If the function fails, the return value is NULL.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Platform.UnsafeNativeMethods.IsClipboardFormatAvailable(System.UInt32)
member.summary: The IsClipboardFormatAvailable function determines whether the clipboard contains data in the specified format.
member.param: Specifies a standard or registered clipboard format.
member.returns: If the clipboard format is available, the return value is nonzero. If the clipboard format is not available, the return value is zero.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Platform.UnsafeNativeMethods.GetClipboardData(System.UInt32)
member.summary: The GetClipboardData function retrieves data from the clipboard in a specified format. The clipboard must have been opened previously.
member.param: Specifies a clipboard format.
member.returns: If the function succeeds, the return value is the handle to a clipboard object in the specified format. If the function fails, the return value is NULL.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Platform.UnsafeNativeMethods.SetClipboardViewer(System.IntPtr)
member.summary: The SetClipboardViewer function adds the specified window to the chain of clipboard viewers. Clipboard viewer windows receive a WM_DRAWCLIPBOARD message whenever the content of the clipboard changes.
member.param: Handle to the window to be added to the clipboard chain.
member.returns: If the function succeeds, the return value identifies the next window in the clipboard viewer chain. If an error occurs or there are no other windows in the clipboard viewer chain, the return value is NULL.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Platform.UnsafeNativeMethods.SetWindowsHookEx(GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Forms.HookType,GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Forms.HookProc,System.IntPtr,System.Int32)
member.summary: The SetWindowsHookEx function installs an application-defined hook procedure into a hook chain. You would install a hook procedure to monitor the system for certain types of events. These events are associated either with a specific thread or with all threads in the same desktop as the calling thread.
member.param: Specifies the type of hook procedure to be installed.

Pointer to the hook procedure. If the threadId parameter is zero or specifies the identifier of a thread created by a different process, the hookProc parameter must point to a hook procedure in a dynamic-link library (DLL). Otherwise, hookProc can point to a hook procedure in the code associated with the current process.

Handle to the DLL containing the hook procedure pointed to by the hookProc parameter. The hInstance parameter must be set to NULL if the threadId parameter specifies a thread created by the current process and if the hook procedure is within the code associated with the current process.

Specifies the identifier of the thread with which the hook procedure is to be associated. If this parameter is zero, the hook procedure is associated with all existing threads running in the same desktop as the calling thread.
member.returns: If the function succeeds, the return value is the handle to the hook procedure. If the function fails, the return value is NULL.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Platform.UnsafeNativeMethods.UnhookWindowsHookEx(System.IntPtr)
member.summary: The UnhookWindowsHookEx function removes a hook procedure installed in a hook chain by the function.
member.param: Handle to the hook to be removed. This parameter is a hook handle obtained by a previous call to .
member.returns: If the function succeeds, the return value is true. If the function fails, the return value is false.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Platform.UnsafeNativeMethods.CallNextHookEx(System.IntPtr,System.Int32,System.IntPtr,System.IntPtr)
member.summary: The CallNextHookEx function passes the hook information to the next hook procedure in the current hook chain. A hook procedure can call this function either before or after processing the hook information.
member.param: Ignored.
Specifies the hook code passed to the current hook procedure. The next hook procedure uses this code to determine how to process the hook information.
Specifies the wParam value passed to the current hook procedure. The meaning of this parameter depends on the type of hook associated with the current hook chain.
Specifies the lParam value passed to the current hook procedure. The meaning of this parameter depends on the type of hook associated with the current hook chain.

summary.newpara: Specifies the appearance of a button.
This enumeration has a attribute that allows a bitwise combination of its member values.

member.remarks:
This enumeration represents the different states of a button.
This is exactly the same as that to the except that it supports other features such as hovering, focus drawing etc.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Framework.Spread.InputMan.CellType.Views.Controls.SingleLineTextEditor.HighlightText
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to highlight text in the control.
member.value: true when control got focus selecte all the text; otherwise false. The default value is false.

remarks.para: This property allows you to highlight all text in the control upon receiving focus.

member.summary: Specifies that national digits are chosen according to the nearest previous strong text, rather than using DefaultLanguage.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Control.InvertPreBoundDir
member.summary: By default, text at the start of the string is laid out as if it follows a strong LTR character if the base embedding level is 0, and as if it follows a strong RTL character if the base embedding level is 1.Set InvertPreBoundDir to change the initial context to the opposite of the base embedding level. This member is for GetCharacterPlacement legacy support.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Control.InvertPostBoundDir
member.summary: By default, text at the end of the string is laid out as if it precedes strong text of the same direction as the base embedding level. Set InvertPreBoundDir to change the final context to the opposite of the base embedding level. This flag is for GetCharacterPlacement legacy support.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Control.LinkStringBefore
member.summary: Causes the first character of the string to be shaped as if it were joined to a previous character.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Control.LinkStringAfter
member.summary: Causes the last character of the string to be shaped as if it were joined to a following character.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Control.NeutralOverride
member.summary: Causes all neutral characters in the string to be treated as if they were strong characters of their enclosing embedding level. This effectively locks them in place, and reordering occurs only between neutrals.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Control.NumericOverride
member.summary: Causes all numeric characters in the string to be treated as if they were strong characters of their enclosing embedding level. This effectively locks them in place, and reordering occurs only between numeric characters.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Control.LegacyBidiClass
member.summary:
Causes the plus and minus characters to be treated as neutral characters, that is, with no implied direction, and the slash character to be treated as a common separator.
Windows XP: The plus and minus characters are treated as European separators.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.State.BidiLevel
member.summary: The embedding level associated with all characters in this run according to the Unicode bidirectional algorithm. When passed to ScriptItemize, should be initialized to zero for an LTR base embedding level, or 1 for RTL.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.State.OverrideDirection
member.summary: true if this level is an override level (LRO/RLO). In an override level, characters are laid out in one direction only, either left-to-right or right-to-left. No reordering of digits or strong characters of opposing direction takes place. Note that this initial value is reset by LRE, RLE, LRO or RLO codes in the string.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.State.InhibitSymSwap
member.summary: True if the shaping engine is to bypass mirroring of Unicode mirrored glyphs such as brackets. Set by Unicode character ISS, cleared by ASS.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.State.CharShape
member.summary: true if character codes in the Arabic Presentation Forms areas of Unicode should be shaped. (Not implemented).

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.State.DigitSubstitute
member.summary: true if character codes U+0030 through U+0039 (European digits) are to be substituted by national digits. Set by Unicode NADS, cleared by NODS.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.State.InhibitLigate
member.summary: true if ligatures are not to be used in the shaping of Arabic or Hebrew characters.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.State.DisplayZWG
member.summary: true if control characters are to be shaped as representational glyphs. (Typically, control characters are shaped to the blank glyph and given a width of zero).

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.State.ArabicNumContext
member.summary: true indicates prior strong characters were Arabic for the purposes of rule P0 as discussed in The Unicode Standard, version 2.0. This should normally be set to true before itemizing an RTL paragraph in an Arabic language, and false otherwise.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.State.GcpClusters
member.summary: For GetCharacterPlacement legacy support only. Initialize to true to request ScriptShape to generate the pwLogClust array the same way as GetCharacterPlacement does in Arabic and Hebrew Windows. Affects only Arabic and Hebrew items.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Analysis.Script
member.summary:
Opaque value identifying which engine Uniscribe will use when calling the ScriptShape, ScriptPlace, and ScriptTextOut functions for this item. The value of eScript is undefined and will change in future releases, but attributes of eScript may be obtained by calling ScriptGetProperties.
To disable shaping, set this parameter to Analysis.UndefinedScript.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Analysis.RTL
member.summary: Rendering direction. Normally identical to the parity of the Unicode embedding level, but it may differ if overridden by GetCharacterPlacement legacy support.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Analysis.LayoutRTL
member.summary: Logical direction, whether left-to-right or right-to-left. Although this is usually the same as fRTL, for a number in a RTL run, fRTL is False (because digits are always displayed LTR), but fLayoutRTL is True (because the number is read as part of the RTL sequence).

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Analysis.LinkBefore
member.summary: If set, the shaping engine will shape the first character of this item as if it were joining with a previous character. Set by ScriptItemize, it may be overridden before calling ScriptShape.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Analysis.LinkAfter
member.summary: If set, the shaping engine will shape the last character of this item as if it were joining with a subsequent character. Set by ScriptItemize, it may be overridden before calling ScriptShape.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Analysis.LogicalOrder
member.summary: If set, the shaping engine will generate all glyph-related arrays in logical order. By default, glyph-related arrays are in visual order, the first array entry corresponding to the leftmost glyph. Set to false by ScriptItemize, it may be overridden before calling ScriptShape.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Analysis.NoGlyphIndex
member.summary:
Typically false. Set to true for bitmap, vector, and device fonts; and for Asian scripts. It may be set to true on input to ScriptShape to disable use of glyphs for this item. Additionally, ScriptShape will set it to true for an hdc containing symbolic, unrecognized, and device fonts.
Disabling glyphing disables complex script shaping. When set, shaping and placing for this item is implemented directly by calls to GetTextExtentExPoint and ExtTextOut.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.LanguageId
member.summary: Primary language and sublanguage associated with the script. When a script is used for many languages, langid represents a default language. For example, Western script is represented by LANG_ENGLISH although it is also used for French, German, and other European languages.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.CharSet
member.summary: The nominal charset associated with the script. This charset may be used in a log font when creating a font suitable for displaying this script. Note that for a new script where no charset is defined, bCharSet may be inappropriate. In this case, DEFAULT_CHARSET should be used instead. See the description of fAmbiguousCharSet.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.Numeric
member.summary: If set, the script contains only digits and the other characters used in writing numbers by the rules of the Unicode bidirectional algorithm. For example, currency symbols, the thousands separator, and the decimal point are classified as numeric when adjacent to or between digits.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.Complex
member.summary: If set, this is a language whose script requires special shaping or layout. If fComplex is false, the script contains no combining characters and requires no contextual shaping or reordering.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.NeedsWordBreaking
member.summary: If set, this is a language whose word break placement requires that the application call ScriptBreak and that word break placement include character positions marked as WordStop in LogicalAttribute. If not set, word break placement is identified by scanning for characters marked as WhiteSpace in LogicalAttribute, or for glyphs marked as Justify == Justification.Blank or Justification.ArabicBlank in VisualAttribute.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.NeedsCaretInfo
member.summary: If set, this is a language that restricts caret placement to cluster boundaries, for example, Thai and Indian. To determine valid caret positions, inspect the CharStop flag in the logical attributes returned by ScriptBreak, or compare adjacent values in the logicClusters array returned by Script.Shape method.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.PrivateUseArea
member.summary: If set, the script uses a special set of characters that is privately defined for the Unicode range U+E000 through U+F8FF.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.NeedsCharacterJustify
member.summary: If set, justification for the script is achieved by increasing the space between all letters, not just between words. When performing inter-character justification, insert extra space only after glyphs marked with VisualAttribute. Justify == Justification.Character.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.InvalidGlyph
member.summary: If set, this is a script for which ScriptShape generates an invalid glyph to represent invalid sequences. That is, it generates wgInvalid in the glyph buffer. The glyph index of the invalid glyph for a particular font may be obtained by calling Script.GetFontProperties method.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.InvalidLogicalAttribute
member.summary: If set, this is a script for which Script.Break marks invalid combinations by setting fInvalid in the logical attributes buffer.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.CDM
member.summary: If set, the script contains an item that was analyzed by Script.Itemize as including Combining Diacritical Marks (U+0300 through U+36F).

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.AmbiguousCharSet
member.summary: If set, the script contains characters that are supported by more than one charset. See the Remarks section for more information. The bCharSet member should be set to DEFAULT_CHARSET.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.ClusterSizeVaries
member.summary: If set, this is a script, such as Arabic, in which contextual shaping may cause a string to increase in size when removing characters. An example of this is Arabic.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.Win.Core.Uniscribe.Properties.RejectInvalid
member.summary: If set, this is a script, such as Thai, where invalid sequences conventionally cause an editor program��such as Notepad��to beep and ignore keystrokes.

If code is greater than or equal to zero, and the hook procedure did not process the message, it is highly recommended that you call CallNextHookEx and return the value it returns; otherwise, other applications that have installed WH_KEYBOARD hooks will not receive hook notifications and may behave incorrectly as a result. member.summary: Gets or sets the percentage used for calculating the color used for the light area of the bevel.
member.value:
An integer value (between -100 through 100) that indicates the lighting percentage.
The default is 25.

remarks.para: This property uses the color ( property) of the object to calculate the light color for the bevel in percentages.
If set to 0, the same color as the color object is used. When a positive value is set, a brighter color is used, and when a negative value is set, a color darker than the background color is used.
This property can be used with the property to make detailed adjustments to the brightness of the bevel color.

member.value:
An integer value (between -100 through 100) that indicates the shading percentage.
The default is -25.

remarks.para: This property uses the color ( property) of the object to calculate the shaded color for the bevel in percentages.
If set to 0, the same color as the color object is used. When a positive value is set, a brighter color is used, and when a negative value is set, a color darker than the color is used.
This property can be used with the property to make detailed adjustments to the brightness of the bevel color.

member.value:
An integer value that indicates the width of the bevel.

member.remarks: When a negative value is set to the Width property, the bevel effect appears Inset, and when a positive value is set, the effect appears Raised. A 2D effect can be achieved by setting the Width property to 0 (zero).

member.summary: Warren Guo add this flag parameter for bug 300 in IM6. This bug is produced by fixing another bug 253 in IM6. The UITypeEditor will call base.Add method then invoke this.OnInsertComplete method. So, we must rollbake to let OnInsertComplete invoke the OnPropertyChanged to make Cantainer layout and refresh. And this flag can support the OnPropertyChanged method only be called one time if user invoke the AddRange method.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Win.Spread.InputMan.CellType.DropDownCalendar.WireCalendarViewEvents
member.summary: Wires the calendar view events.
member.remarks:
NOTE : Please don't suprise when you found that there is no responding "UnWireCalendarViewEvents" method. The reason is all these registered events of CalendarView is in the scope of this DropDownCalendar object, when it is diposed by GC, all the thing in it will be disposed automatically. So, it's unnecessary to logout the registered events.
--- Aaron commented on 2007-05-31

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Win.Spread.InputMan.CellType.DropDownEditor.ScrollToCaret
member.summary: Scrolls the contents of the control to the current caret position.
member.remarks:
This method enables you to scroll the contents of the control until the caret is within the visible region of the control. If the caret is positioned below the visible region of the control, the ScrollToCaret method will scroll the contents of the control until the caret is visible at the bottom of the control. If the caret is positioned above the visible region of the control, this method scrolls the contents of the control until the caret is visible at the top of the control. A similar policy exists for the horizontal direction and it moves the caret to 1/3 width from the left or right side. You can use this method in a multiline edit to ensure that the current text entry point is within the visible region of the control.
Note: This method has no effect if the control does not have focus or if the caret is already positioned in the visible region of the control.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Win.Spread.InputMan.CellType.DropDownEditor.SelectAll
member.summary: Selects all text in the control.
member.remarks: This method enables you to select all text within the control. You can use this method in conjunction with the Cut method, which requires text to be selected in the control, to cut the entire contents of the control and paste them into the Clipboard.

member.remarks: This method will undo the last clipboard or text change operation performed in the control if the CanUndo property returns true.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.Win.Spread.InputMan.CellType.DropDownEditor.WrieEditorViewEvents
member.summary: Wries the editor view events.
member.remarks:
NOTE : Please don't suprise when you found that there is no responding "UnWrieEditorViewEvents" method. The reason is all these registered events of EditorView is in the scope of this DropDownEditor object, when it is diposed by GC, all the thing in it will be disposed automatically. So, it's unnecessary to logout the registered events.
--- Aaron commented on 2007-05-31
